rationale.text: The test has two requirements: the alternative of a non-text element updated by a script is updated, and the updated alternative is relevant. Relevance is judgment. The first requirement could look mechanical, for example an image whose source a script changes while its alt attribute stays the same, but it is not claimed. Seeing the update needs the element to be observed before and after it, which happens only after an interaction or over time. The test applies only to elements that have an alternative, and the official text does not say which forms count; an alternative given by other means than the alt attribute (adjacent text, a caption, a description) may be updated where a check would not look. And whether a given change of the element is an update of its non-text content, rather than the same image served at another address, is not decided by the text. What would raise this: a technique that observes the update, and a closed list of the alternatives the test means. No axe rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is judgment: whether a script updates a non-text element is not known from the page as loaded. Needs is state, since the update follows a script action, usually after an interaction.
